name: Cassandra Collins
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember pinning cloth in a shop barely wider than the mirror.” Monday often includes a stop at the corner by Juniper Tailor, where Cassandra looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I am the daughter. Dad has offered me a valuable building with his office on the top floor.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. Cassandra has fine brows over wide-set eyes, with a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow. Cassandra folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing during a conversation.
personality: Cassandra finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To get a modest tailoring space under personal control.
family: Freya King is Cassandra’s older cousin. Cassandra calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Freya leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The bitter orange*, Freya says, “I brought her son in expecting tears. He ordered something completely different and made everyone laugh.”
connections: Joseph Moran (father). A wealthy father and a young tailor disagree about whether owning a whole building constitutes freedom. Also in the story is Marin Brady (master tailor).

reactions.situation: A tenant hears about the building sale secondhand
reactions.response: Cassandra gives the tenant a reliable contact for the sale information and a real date to expect an answer.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Cassandra asks the counter staff for a receipt so its return can be traced even after their shift changes.
